Days after yet another stranger-on-stranger subway murder rattled New Yorkers, the governor and the mayor stood together to reassure commuters.

“We will do whatever it takes to make our subways safer,” vowed Gov. Kathy Hochul.

Oops: Hochul didn’t make these remarks last week.

She made them four years ago.

The subways today aren’t much safer — but Hochul, on the eve of another re-election, is hoping you’re exhausted by the topic.

This year looks eerily like 2022: In little more than two weeks, two innocent commuters lost their lives in unprovoked attacks.

Preventable attacks: Both incidents show the cost of a lenient criminal-justice system.

On Sept. 30, construction worker Mesias Lojano lost his life on a Queens J train after Jyrell Thomas allegedly stabbed him repeatedly.

Weeks earlier, police had arrested Thomas for shoplifting at a Bronx Target, and for fleeing arrest — but under laws that Hochul supports, a judge released him.

On Oct. 17 Darrel Rodriguez, coming home from his security job, was shot to death on a Midtown subway platform, allegedly by 17-year-old Xavian Collins.

Collins was reportedly smoking pot in the station, and Rodriguez told him to knock it off.

Because the state goes easy on juvenile offenders — under another policy Hochul supports — we can’t know if police had arrested Collins before.

But the killing itself is exactly the kind of case that broken-windows policing was invented to prevent.

A masked and hooded kid toking in the subway is exhibiting antisocial behavior.

Once upon a time, cops could have arrested him for the smaller infraction — and prevented a killing.

Except: We’ve stopped arresting people for smoking pot altogether.

And Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s NYPD is doing less criminal enforcement in transit this year, period.

Through mid-October 2026, transit arrests are down 5% year-over-year, and farebeating arrests down 14%.

Not coincidentally, crime is up.

Serious subway violence is up 6%, and seven people have been murdered, up from four last year.

Things really aren’t better than they were in 2022, when Hochul, in a close race against GOP challenger Lee Zeldin, stood with then-Mayor Eric Adams and trumpeted more cops, more cameras and more mental-health support in the subways.

Back then, through August (the latest month for which year-by-year comparisons are available), subway riders and workers suffered 783 violent felonies — compared to 722 for the same period this year.

That’s 8% fewer, sure — but the problem, four years ago and now, is how much worse things are this decade, compared to the safety that persisted for a generation before 2020.

Today’s incessant felony violence remains 27% above the pre-pandemic levels of 2019.

Another measure: Rodriguez’s killing was the 50th subway murder since March 2020.

Over not quite seven years, we’ve suffered a level of killings that, before 2020, took 22 years to rack up.

In 2022, we ended up with 10 subway murders, a modern record (matched in 2024).

With the seven killings so far in 2026, we’re not far off.

Hochul, on her third mayor, has never figured out how to deal with recidivist criminals and the severely mentally ill.

With Adams as mayor, she pushed the NYPD to flood the subways, paying for the overtime with state funds.

And when cops do apprehend perps, they’re quickly released.

The man who allegedly killed the elderly Ross Falzone in May by pushing him down a flight of Chelsea subway steps had left Bellevue Hospital hours before.

The real difference between this year and 2022 is that Hochul doesn’t see a need to reassure the public.

Yes, she had a press conference with Mamdani last week, after Rodriguez’s murder — but it was focused on her new favorite topic, child care.

When asked later about subway violence, she lamely claimed that “it seems a lot more scary in scale” than it is.

Meanwhile the Metropolitan Transportation Authority, which Hochul oversees, last week halted the civilian fare-enforcement teams it had been dispatching to city buses.

Civilians clearly aren’t equipped to do this job; armed, trained police must do it.

So how many bus fare-evasion tickets has Mamdani’s NYPD written so far this year, compared to 2025’s year-to-date 1,053?

It gets worse — after a recent month of inactivity, in which the NYPD issued zero bus tickets, it erased the line altogether from its regular CompStat report.

Under Mamdani, the NYPD has quiet-quit the fare-enforcement business.

Hochul is betting that voters have gotten used to what once would have been an unacceptable level of subway crime; that they’re too concerned about inflation and unaffordability.

Next week, we’ll find out if she’s right.

Nicole Gelinas is a contributing editor to the Manhattan Institute’s City Journal and a 2026 Moynihan Center fellow. Opinions are her own and not her employer’s.

Stanford University has been embroiled in another AI image controversy after it was forced to remove an image of an all-white, all-male marching band from its website following an outcry from students.

The AI-generated picture, published on the prestigious US university’s Campus Center construction website, showed a band dressed in red blazers, white shirts and fedoras performing on the campus’ White Plaza.

Members of the Leland Stanford Junior University Marching Band told The Stanford Daily they were shocked to find the AI-generated image on the university’s website.

Drum major Jose Serrano called the decision “pretty stupid.”

“If you’re going to use AI, make an AI thing for your building, but don’t put people on it,” he said.

Band conductor and executive officer Sadie Taylor said the depiction was particularly frustrating, given the organization’s efforts to attract a diverse membership.

“We work pretty hard to champion diversity within the organization and try and encourage women and students of color to join,” she said. “So to see the University sort of undo all of that, it’s pretty frustrating.”

Taylor and fellow band leaders formally complained to the Campus Center team on Monday, pointing out that authentic photographs of the band were already available.

“We welcome you to use one of those, instead of falsifying an all-white, all-male, AI slop version of the Band,” they wrote.

The university replaced the image with another architectural rendering shortly afterward.

Taylor said the university had not informed the band before publishing the image, while Serrano questioned the use of AI to generate figures resembling real students without their knowledge.

“Our likenesses are being put into this AI algorithm and spit out and spat out, which is just ridiculous. It’s insane,” he said.

Stanford defended the image as an architectural visualization intended to illustrate Commons Great Room, part of the wider Campus Center redevelopment.

Assistant Vice President of Communications Angie Davis said the figures were illustrative and were not intended to represent members of the marching band.

“AI-assisted imagery is standard industry practice for architectural visualization,” Davis wrote in an email to The Stanford Daily.

However, band members said the figures’ clothing closely resembled their distinctive uniforms, with some claiming the generated figures looked like actual members.

Stanford’s AI guidelines prohibit generating “content that depicts, impersonates, or closely resembles a real person.” The university has not said the marching band image breached those guidelines.

The latest controversy follows a separate incident in September, when Stanford admitted it had breached its own AI policies by digitally altering a photograph used in promotional material.

Hispanic student Billy Ramirez was removed from a photograph taken at a Lunar New Year celebration in 2024 and replaced with an AI-generated black woman. Two other students in the image were digitally altered to appear thinner.

The changes, first reported by student publication The Stanford Review, prompted the university to remove the promotional banners.

“Both the alteration and lack of disclosure in this case violate that policy,” Stanford said in a statement, adding that it would provide additional training and strengthen reviews of promotional material.

Ramirez described the experience as upsetting.

“To see me erased like that so easily was kind of very upsetting,” he said.

Stanford’s policy prohibits using AI to produce or alter images of university people, events, research, facilities or achievements.

While the university acknowledged a policy breach in Ramirez’s case, it defended the marching band image as an illustrative rendering rather than a depiction of identifiable people.

پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. دانشگاه استنفورد پس از اینکه مجبور شد تصویری از یک گروه راهپیمایی کاملاً سفید و کاملاً مرد را در پی اعتراض دانشجویان حذف کند، درگیر بحث دیگری درباره تصویر هوش مصنوعی شده است. تصویر تولید شده توسط هوش مصنوعی که در وب سایت ساختمانی مرکز پردیس دانشگاه معتبر ایالات متحده منتشر شد، گروهی را با لباس های کت قرمز، پیراهن های سفید و فدورا نشان می دهد که در وایت پلازای پردیس هنرنمایی می کنند. اعضای گروه راهپیمایی دانشگاه Leland Stanford Junior به The Stanford Daily گفتند که از دیدن بزرگترین اخبار مربوط به افکار و عقاید دانشگاه در حال حاضر در وب سایت فرهنگی درست دانشگاه، شوکه شده اند. لطفاً یک ایمیل معتبر ارائه دهید. با کلیک بر روی بالا، با شرایط استفاده و سیاست حفظ حریم خصوصی موافقت می کنید. خوزه سرانو، سرگرد درام، این تصمیم را "بسیار احمقانه" نامید.
او گفت: «اگر می‌خواهید از هوش مصنوعی استفاده کنید، یک چیز هوش مصنوعی برای ساختمان خود بسازید، اما افراد را در آن قرار ندهید.» سدی تیلور، رهبر گروه و مدیر اجرایی، گفت که این تصویر به‌ویژه با توجه به تلاش‌های سازمان برای جذب اعضای متنوع، خسته‌کننده بود. او گفت: "ما سخت کار می کنیم تا از تنوع در سازمان حمایت کنیم و تلاش می کنیم زنان و دانش آموزان رنگین پوست را به پیوستن تشویق کنیم." "بنابراین دیدن دانشگاه که همه اینها را به نوعی خنثی می کند، بسیار خسته کننده است."
تیلور و رهبران گروه دیگر به طور رسمی به تیم مرکز پردیس شکایت کردند و اشاره کردند که عکس‌های معتبر گروه قبلاً منتشر شده است.

Theo Edema was pressed into action Sunday against one of the best centers in the country, and the freshman performed better than anyone could have expected.

Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Zach Braziller about the inside buzz on St. John’s.

With starting big man Ruben Prey in foul trouble, Edema logged 12 minutes. He shined, notching four points, seven rebounds (four offensive), a block and a steal in St. John’s 84-74 win over Texas in the Red Storm’s exhibition finale.

The 6-foot-11, 255-pound Edema held his own against 7-foot Longhorns center Matas Vokietaitis.

“He was big down the stretch, he wouldn’t let them get back in the game with offensive rebounds,” coach Rick Pitino said.

A four-star prospect, Edema committed to St. John’s in May, picking the Johnnies over Maryland, BYU and Stanford. He was supposed to be a high school senior this year but reclassified to attend college early. Edema could become a key part of the second unit.

“He played amazing. I’m a big fan of his game,” Tounde Yessoufou said. “His energy. You can tell he affects the game in many different types of ways. He got some good blocks, he was a dog on defense. That’s something we really, really need.”

Quinn Ellis ended three preseason games with three turnovers in 116 minutes.

He also has 22 assists. Pitino heaped praise on his point guard after he tallied four points, seven assists, three rebounds and no turnovers in 34 minutes against Texas.

“Quinn dominated the game without scoring and Ian [Jackson] benefits so much. That’s a terrific backcourt. I thought Quinn dominated the game today, got the ball moving and got everyone involved in the game,” Pitino said. “On this basketball team, Quinn is so key, because everyone wants to score, and Quinn doesn’t really care about that.

“He cares about winning, he cares about doing the right things, he cares about playing good defense. He’s really a great point guard to have with this basketball team.”

“This is what happens when nations let wealth and power accumulate in the hands of a few,” says prospective 2028 presidential candidate Rep. Ro Khanna about the mass rioting and social unrest unfolding in France.

As with most issues, the far-left Californian has it backward: The economic and social ideas dear to his own Democratic Party are what have destabilized France.

France, after all, is home to socialized medicine, high minimum wages, powerful unions, some of the most generous worker protections in the world, big government spending and a massive welfare state.

France’s Gini index, the standard measure of income inequality, is just under 32, around the European Union average.

Of course income inequality, the hobbyhorse of the American left, is completely irrelevant in and of itself; France ranks right in the middle worldwide by that measure, between the stable and wealthy Western democracy of Japan and the destitute Asian tyranny of Myanmar.

Rioters didn’t set fire to the majestic 19th-century Limoges town hall because they’re angry about France’s ranking in global income parity.

They were triggered in large part by the French government’s alleged “austerity” plans.

France spends an inordinate amount of its budget on welfare and social protection programs — a larger percentage than virtually any nation on Earth.

Since 1995, social and welfare spending has risen from 53% to nearly 59% of the country’s budget.

It will never be enough for rioters.

Because such a significant percentage of its budget is dedicated to keeping the welfare state operational, any reforms aimed at reducing spending or debt will be greeted with immediate social turmoil.

France’s public debt is approaching 120% of gross domestic product, and is projected to rise to around 122% soon.

The government recently proposed reducing the budget deficit from an expected 5.4% of GDP in 2026 to 5% in 2027.

In other words, young French people are destroying their cities over a proposed deficit reduction of 0.4 percentage points of GDP.

To pay for this system, France has among the highest tax rates in the developed world.

Employer social security contributions average around 45% of gross salary, while employee contributions add another 22% to 25%.

The tax on consumer goods is 20%.

That’s a heavy burden for productive members of French society.

But over 50% of French households don’t pay any income tax: Despite benefiting from the system, they are untethered from the responsibilities of paying for it.

Other nations with generous social welfare programs, such as Denmark, also have high levels of social cohesion, and virtually every household pays some income tax.

“We spend too much money, and we strip people of responsibility,” President Emmanuel Macron said back in 2018.

“An insane amount we spend on minimal welfare payments, but people are still poor . . . We have to do something to get people out of this situation.”

France has one of the highest unemployment rates in Europe and one of the lowest retirement ages.

Youth unemployment is over 21%; it’s 9% in the United States, and we rightly consider it a problem.

Unemployment among Muslim youth is far higher — and over 34% of France’s young people have immigrant parents or grandparents, most from Muslim-majority countries.

Over 15% of the population in the Paris metropolitan area is Muslim.

And despite the media’s best efforts to convince us otherwise, plenty of the recent violence appears to be connected to Muslim immigrants and the nihilistic Palestinianism that Khanna champions.

Riots will radicalize politics.

Many French people detest anarchy, which might bode well for right-wing opposition leader Marine Le Pen in the next election — but should she succeed, that too will almost surely lead to more social unrest.

It’s true that the French have never needed much excuse to riot.

France saw major social unrest every year from 2005 through 2009, then in 2018 and 2019, in 2023, in 2025 and again this year.

Many of those riots have been driven by reliance on government handouts or by Muslims living in the Paris suburbs.

The more you hook people on state dependency, the less likely they are to break free of it.

The more unassimilated people and illiberal ideas you import into your country, the less social cohesion you’ll get.

France is the future Ro Khanna imagines for us.

David Harsanyi is a senior writer at the Washington Examiner. X: @davidharsanyi
news.content: رو خانا نامزد احتمالی ریاست جمهوری 2028 در مورد شورش های جمعی و ناآرامی های اجتماعی در حال وقوع در فرانسه می گوید: «این همان چیزی است که وقتی ملت ها اجازه می دهند ثروت و قدرت در دستان معدودی انباشته شود، اتفاق می افتد.» مانند بسیاری از مسائل، کالیفرنیای چپ افراطی آن چیزی است که ایده دموکرات های فرانسه را به عقب انداخته است. به هر حال، فرانسه خانه پزشکی اجتماعی شده، حداقل دستمزدهای بالا، اتحادیه‌های قدرتمند، برخی از سخاوتمندانه‌ترین حمایت‌های کارگران در جهان، هزینه‌های کلان دولت و یک دولت رفاهی عظیم است. شاخص جینی فرانسه، معیار استاندارد نابرابری درآمد، کمی کمتر از 32 است، در حدود میانگین اتحادیه اروپا. البته نابرابری درآمد، اسب سرگرمی چپ آمریکایی، به خودی خود کاملاً بی ربط است. فرانسه با این معیار در سراسر جهان درست در وسط قرار دارد، بین دموکراسی باثبات و ثروتمند غربی ژاپن و ظلم فقیر آسیایی میانمار. آشوبگران ساختمان شهری باشکوه قرن نوزدهمی لیموژ را آتش نزدند زیرا از رتبه فرانسه در برابری درآمد جهانی عصبانی هستند. آنها تا حد زیادی توسط برنامه‌های "ریاضت اقتصادی" ادعایی دولت فرانسه آغاز شده‌اند. فرانسه مقدار زیادی از بودجه خود را صرف برنامه‌های رفاهی و حمایت اجتماعی می‌کند - درصدی بیشتر از هر کشور روی زمین. از سال 1995، هزینه‌های اجتماعی و رفاهی از 53٪ به تقریباً 59٪ بودجه کشور افزایش یافته است.

An LA actor and comedian who has appeared in roles alongside Jake Gyllenhaal and Mark Ruffalo threatened to cut the jugular of a man living with his ex before hitting him with a shovel and attempting to run him over with his car, according to a new lawsuit.

Alleged victim Lucas Scheerer is describing the details of the horrific broad daylight attack in West Hollywood on August 4 by funny man Eliot Preschutti in the bombshell papers filed Friday in LA Superior Court.

Scheerer was living at the home of Preschutti’s former romantic partner, Michelle Farrell, when the comedian came to the residence and attacked him around noon, per the suit.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

The actor threw Sheerer to the ground and threatened to cut his jugular and kill him, the documents state. Preschutti then grabbed a garden shovel and hit Scheerer on the neck with it, cutting him and then attempted to run him over with his car.

Scheerer was rushed to a trauma unit at Cedars-Sinai Hospital where he received emergency treatment.

The victim “suffered serious bodily injuries including to his head and neck and great physical, mental, and emotional pain and suffering,” the suit reads.

Preschutti was arrested, the status of the case is unclear. Preschutti was arrested and booked into the West Hollywood Station jail on an attempted murder charge, jail records listed his bail at $2 million, WeHoTimes reported.

The Post’s attempts to reach Preschutti for comment were not returned. The Post requested an update on charges from the LA District Attorney’s office but is yet to hear back.

Preschutti and Farrell have been in a years-long battle over the West Hollywood property where the incident took place, The Post has learned.

Preschutti is accused of holding a knife to Ferrell’s throat in the bathroom according to a civil suit involving ownership of the residence. Both claim to be full owners.

“On August 23, 2022, Preschutti forced Farrell to sign the Deed Contract against her will at knife point to her throat, saying ‘if you don’t sign this, I’m going to kill you and your children’,” the lawsuit claims.

The legal documents go on to say: “He drove her against her will to Wells Fargo where she was forced to sign with the notary.”

“She signed under threats, duress, and criminal activity of Preschutti to induce her to sign for fear of her own safety and the safety of her children,” the suit adds.

The papers also point to other violent episodes. “In or about January 2024, Preschutti hit a female security guard in the face at the Comedy Store, and the male security took him down,” they read.

Preschutti has also been banned from entering some of the Sunset Strip’s most well-known clubs including the Rainbow Room, Comedy Store, and Barney’s Beanery “because of his drunken violent nature,” the papers say.

The actor has uncredited scenes in the movie South Paw with Jake Gyllenhaal and Foxcatcher with Mark Ruffalo. The Post contacted Preschutti for comment.

Scheerer’s lawsuit also names Farrell, claiming premises liability. Farrell was also contacted for comment.

Scheerer is seeking economic damages for medical, hospital, and incidental expenses to be determined by a jury.

news.originalContent:
The Department of Justice has faced criticism that its lawsuit is aimed at blocking a Democratic victory in a key race.

United States Attorney General Todd Blanche has defended the Department of Justice’s decision to sue to prevent the certification of a Republican loss in Alaska’s tight Senate race.

On Sunday, Blanche did a tour of the morning political shows in the US, making stops at CNN’s State of the Union TV programme and CBS’s Face the Nation.

In each appearance, he faced pointed questions about the legality of the Justice Department’s efforts, responding, in some cases, with open frustration.

“ Why is this controversial?” Blanche asked CNN host Dana Bash at one point. He proceeded to accuse one of the candidates in the Senate race of intentionally trying to confuse voters.

“We’re going to try to create a situation where that can be remedied,” he said. “That shouldn’t be something that is causing this shock and horror.”

But the Justice Department’s lawsuit, filed on October 22, has been the subject of bipartisan criticism.

Many have accused the administration of President Donald Trump of laying the groundwork to block a Democratic win in the race. Trump himself claimed to have authorised the lawsuit.

“I’m the one who said do it,” he told reporters on Friday.

During the midterm elections on November 3, citizens in Alaska will be asked to vote in one of the closest Senate races in the country, one which will help decide whether Republicans maintain their majority in the chamber.

Senator Dan S Sullivan, the Republican incumbent, is seeking to defend his seat in the Senate. But he faces fierce competition from former US Representative Mary Peltola, a Democrat.

Also in the running is another candidate named Dan J Sullivan, a former Forest Service employee.

The second Sullivan’s decision to also run has raised concerns that he is a spoiler candidate, whose presence on the ballot is designed to draw votes away from the incumbent.

But the Forest Service worker has denied any such intent. Such allegations, he said, are “entirely false”.

“I am not a registered Democrat, and I have had no conversations whatsoever with the Peltola campaign about my candidacy,” the second Sullivan wrote in a letter to Alaska’s lieutenant governor before the state’s primaries.

“I have considered running for political office for over a decade. I made the decision to formally run for the United States Senate in the upcoming primary election because Senator Sullivan has routinely failed the people of Alaska, and they deserve a better representative. It is my right to do so.”

Four candidates advanced to the final round of voting after Alaska’s August primaries. They included Peltola and both Sullivans. The two men are running as Republicans.

The Department of Justice has argued that its lawsuit — filed less than two weeks before the midterm elections — is necessary “to protect the integrity” of the election.

Any result in the Senate race, it argues, would be “tainted by the inclusion on the ballot of Daniel J Sullivan”.

The department has therefore called on the US district court in Alaska to issue an order declaring the race’s certification “unlawful” and barring the state from “allowing such a certification to occur”.

Under the US Constitution, only states have the power to administer elections, though Congress has the right to pass regulations concerning federal votes.

It is highly unusual for a presidential administration to inject itself into issues of state election certification — and experts say such a move is likely to be deemed illegal.

Already, in June, Alaska’s Supreme Court ruled that both Sullivans could compete in the Senate race. The state’s Division of Elections has also taken steps to reduce voter confusion.

The November 3 ballot, for instance, will list Dan S Sullivan as the incumbent and as a “registered Republican”.

Dan J Sullivan, meanwhile, will have the suffix “Jr” added to his name, and his party affiliation will be left blank, despite the candidate identifying as Republican.

But in Sunday’s TV appearances, Blanche — who leads the Department of Justice and formerly served as Trump’s personal lawyer — argued that merely having two Sullivans on the ballot is a recipe for confusion.

“It is wrong,” Blanche told CNN. “Putting aside whether we’re going to win or lose in the courts, putting aside what the Alaskan Supreme Court has done, in our system we should not have a candidate who has to worry about another candidate being on the ballot for no other reason than to confuse voters.”

Blanche also denied any impropriety in Trump saying he ordered the lawsuit.

“He’s supposed to make sure that everything in this country is running right, including elections,” Blanche said.

Historically, the Department of Justice has embraced a norm of judicial independence, though critics have accused the Trump administration of wielding its prosecutorial powers for political gain.

Bash, the CNN host, raised some of those concerns, pointing to Trump’s comments accusing Democrats of cheating, as well as his history of election denialism.

The president has long denied his loss in the 2020 presidential race, and his supporters sought to block the certification of that election, notably by storming the US Capitol on January 6, 2021.

When Bash pointed to that incident, Blanche chided her: “Oh, you’ve got to stop it with that.”

“Why are you yelling at me?” Bash responded, as the two talked over each other.

“You are not being a real person. Come on, man,” Blanche continued. “That is crazy.”

He also denied that Trump was setting the stage for a contested election if the Democrat Peltola were to win. Instead, he framed the lawsuit as setting the stage for further investigations into any eventual results.

“The relief that we’re seeking — which, again, isn’t to determine who the senator is, it’s not to try to overturn something the state is going to do — it’s just to make sure that the ballots that come in are kept in a way that may allow a court to investigate further,” Blanche said.

Speaking to CBS, Blanche also dodged a question about whether Trump personally asked him to file the lawsuit.

“I will never, ever, ever talk about communications that I have with the president of the United States. I never have, and I never will,” Blanche said.

The race to control the US Senate is expected to be a nail-biter, with the Republicans holding a slim majority at present: They have 53 seats in the 100-member chamber.

Only a third of the Senate’s seats — 35 in total — will be up for grabs in the midterm races, though, as terms in the chamber last six years and are staggered across different election years.

Trump’s Republican Party is projected to face an uphill battle to protect its congressional majorities, amid backlash against the rising cost of living and Trump’s own withering poll numbers.

Roughly seven Senate elections are considered toss-ups, including the Alaska race.

In early October, The New York Times and Siena College released a poll finding Peltola leading the incumbent Sullivan by nearly seven percentage points, one of the widest margins of any of the toss-up states.

وزارت دادگستری با انتقاداتی مواجه شده است که هدف از شکایت آن جلوگیری از پیروزی دموکرات ها در یک رقابت کلیدی است. تاد بلانچ، دادستان کل ایالات متحده از تصمیم وزارت دادگستری برای شکایت برای جلوگیری از تأیید شکست جمهوری خواهان در رقابت تنگاتنگ سنا در آلاسکا دفاع کرده است. روز یکشنبه، بلانش توری از برنامه‌های سیاسی صبحگاهی در ایالات متحده داشت و در برنامه تلویزیونی CNN و Face the Nation شبکه سی‌بی‌اس به سر می‌برد. او در هر حضور، با پرسش‌هایی در مورد قانونی بودن تلاش‌های وزارت دادگستری مواجه می‌شد که در برخی موارد با ناامیدی آشکار پاسخ می‌داد.» چرا این بحث برانگیز است؟» بلانش در یک نقطه از مجری CNN دانا باش پرسید. او یکی از نامزدهای انتخابات سنا را متهم به تلاش عمدی برای گیج کردن رأی دهندگان کرد. او گفت: «ما سعی خواهیم کرد شرایطی ایجاد کنیم که بتوان آن را اصلاح کرد. "این نباید چیزی باشد که باعث این شوک و وحشت شود."
اما شکایت وزارت دادگستری که در 22 اکتبر تنظیم شد، موضوع انتقادات دو حزبی بوده است. بسیاری دولت دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور آمریکا را متهم کرده اند که زمینه را برای جلوگیری از پیروزی دموکرات ها در رقابت های انتخاباتی فراهم کرده است. ترامپ خود مدعی شد که مجوز این شکایت را داده است. او روز جمعه به خبرنگاران گفت: «من کسی هستم که گفتم این کار را انجام بده.» در طول انتخابات میان دوره ای در 3 نوامبر، از شهروندان آلاسکا خواسته می شود تا در یکی از نزدیک ترین رقابت های سنا در این کشور رای دهند، انتخاباتی که به تصمیم گیری در مورد حفظ اکثریت جمهوری خواهان کمک می کند.

They’ve opened the season by making a statement with wins over the Spurs and Nuggets. The 2025 champions are showing they’re serious about reaching the mountaintop again after getting eliminated by the Spurs in the 2026 Western Conference Finals.

LeBron James and company look like the real deal after beating the defending champion Knicks as well as the Celtics. James, who’s turning 42 years old this season, could actually win his fifth championship if the 76ers keep this up.

Their 0-2 start isn’t great. But they’re the defending champions and deserve to be near the top of these rankings until proven otherwise.

There will be some growing pains integrating a three-guard rotation. But it won’t be long until they figure it out. Wemby carried this team to the Finals last year and he’s expected to carry them far again.

This team might’ve been slept on entering the season. Fred VanVleet is back and Kevin Durant, Alperen Sengun, Amen Thompson and Jabari Smith Jr. are looking dangerous. The Rockets could be a dark horse in the West.

This team’s success is going to hinge on Walker Kessler. And Kessler is looking good.

Anthony Edwards is so much fun. He opened this season with a 45-point performance against the Heat. When he and LaMelo Ball figure things out, the Timberwolves could make some real noise.

Scottie Barnes, RJ Barrett, Kawhi Leonard and Immanuel Quickley can’t be slept on this season. The Raptors’ starters combined for 92 points to beat the Bulls by 43 points in their opening game.

They’re looking good but were dealt a blow when Jalen Duren suffered a right hamstring strain. He’s going to be reevaluated in two weeks, which means the team is going to face a very tough stretch without him, including playing the 76ers twice and the Knicks.

Paul George had a 38-point performance in the Celtics’ loss to the Pistons in their season-opener, followed by Jayson Tatum scoring 36 points in a win over the Knicks. The Celtics’ stars are looking ready to go.

This team has a great starting lineup. But not much depth.

12. Portland Trail Blazers

Welcome back, Dame. We missed you. Lillard has seemingly found his rhythm after missing last season because of a torn left Achilles’ tendon. Lillard, Deni Avdija and Toumani Camara are going to be a lot of fun this season.

The 19-year-old Cam Boozer already looks like an All-Star. In his second NBA game, he finished with 25 points, 13 rebounds, six assists and two steals in a win over the Warriors.

The Cavaliers will need more scoring from James Harden, who’s averaging 14 points over two games, if they’re going to make any noise in the East.

Kyrie Irving and Cooper Flagg could be dangerous when they find a rhythm alongside one another. They’ve had a tough opening schedule, with losses to the Spurs and Rockets. But this team has a lot of promise.

We’ve learned not to underestimate Tyrese Haliburton after he led the Pacers to the Finals in 2025. This team will always be dangerous with him on it.

The Heat are off to a rough start at 0-3. But Bam Adebayo hasn’t looked like himself. We’re still optimistic that he and Giannis Antetokounmpo will figure things out, though.

The Hawks beat the Magic and Hornets and a lot of guys are making contributions. They have a lot of promise on both sides of the court.

Love seeing Naz Reid balling out for the Hornets. He’s averaging career-highs in points (20), rebounds (8.7) and assists (three) in his team’s three games, including wins over the Heat and Nets and a loss against the Hawks.

An 0-2 start isn’t what Paolo Banchero, Franz Wagner and Jalen Suggs had in mind. This team better get things together or it’s going to be a long season.

A 20-point loss to the Grizzlies in their season-opener wasn’t on their bingo card. But it’s early and I expect Lauri Markkanen to get his act together soon.

They lost to the Trail Blazers by 41 points in their season-opener. Still stunned by that. But Devin Booker redeemed himself with a 43-point performance against the Warriors on Saturday.

Trae Young and Anthony Davis both have a lot to prove. This team is a wildcard. They could exceed expectations…or flounder. They’ve only really been tested by the Raptors so far in a 112-102 loss. This is a team to keep your eye on.

Caleb Wilson has lived up to expectations, averaging 22.3 points and eight rebounds in three games. His Rookie of the Year campaign has officially begun.

They’re missing so many guys, but Darius Garland looks like he’s back in All-Star mode, which is nice to see after he was hampered by injuries last season.

26.  Golden State Warriors

Things aren’t looking great for this injury-riddled team that’s without Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody moody for the first few months of the season and Kristaps Porzingis indefinitely. But they still have Steph Curry and Draymond Green. And Yaxel Lendeborg is a ton of fun on and off the court, including recently making waves for saying he lost all respect for Luka Doncic.

The Pelicans are off to an 0-3 start, though they did take the Nuggets to overtime in a game on Saturday. It appears to be the same old sad story for this team.

It’s going to be a long season for the Kings, who currently have the second-worst offensive rating in the NBA (102.4).

They’re in rebuild mode, but Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr. are still fun to watch.

Goodbye Giannis. Hello dark days.

The retired NYPD narcotics detective accused of gunning down a driver in a horrifying road rage incident on the George Washington Bridge last week is out of jail after posting $1 million bail.

Victor Romero, 62, posted the seven-figure sum on Friday, according to Department of Correction records — three days after he allegedly shot and killed Con Ed worker Koran Irvine in a drive-by shooting on the busy span and fled the scene.

Romero was initially charged with murder, but his charges were downgraded to manslaughter — to the shock of family members and friends of the beloved 46-year-old father of two.

“I think if he was charged with murder, he should have been remanded without bail,” Irvine family attorney Keith White told The Post on Sunday.

“In most serious cases involving suspects that should be charged with murder, people are remanded,” White explained. “But also, I have cases where people aren’t charged with murder, they’re charged with lesser crimes, and they are remanded as a flight risk.”

Romero and Irvine — who both lived in Rockland County — had almost collided during a lane change on the ramp to the upper level of the outbound bridge, sources said.

Romero then allegedly tailed Irvine’s sedan before pulling up to the passenger side of Irvine’s vehicle, and firing a single shot through the window — striking the Con Ed worker in the shoulder — and driving off.

He was arrested the next day on murder charges that were quickly downgraded without explanation at his Thursday arraignment, even as prosecutors called the case “particularly senseless.”

Outside Manhattan Criminal Court, about a dozen family members and friends of Irvine said they believed the ex-cop was given preferential treatment by the court system, concerns echoed by White.

“So somebody who chases down and kills somebody in a car, and then flees the scene, doesn’t call 911 isn’t deemed a flight risk?” the lawyer asked rhetorically.

Irvine’s loved ones are not doing well as they grapple with the news of Romero’s release while making funeral plans, sources close to the family said.

The New York City Police Pension Fund public database had withheld information about the value of retirement payments for Romero, who left the job in 2001.

He had been working as a driver for the CEO of the multi-billion-dollar biotech and energy investment firm QVT Financial and was behind the wheel of the company’s Range Rover SUV when he allegedly fatally shot Irvine.

Romero is due back in court on Tuesday, court records show.

While the Atlanta Falcons gave the San Francisco 49ers their first loss of the season on Sunday, wide receiver Drake London did not appear too happy during the middle of it.

With 5:24 left in the third quarter and a 19-14 lead over San Francisco, London was seen yelling at one of the referees during the game.

WOW: #Falcons superstar WR Drake London yelled “YOU A B*TCH” toward a referee from the sideline after a helmet-to-helmet collision against the #49ers.London was furious following the play and did not hold back.LONDON WAS PISSED OFF.😳😳😳  pic.twitter.com/Ij6vwH0VbE

It’s unknown what exactly London said, but speculation on social media suggests that he said, “You a b—h!”

The video started off with London talking to a member of the Falcons organization on the sideline, then walking down and turning his head back at the last second to voice his frustration at the official.

Before the heated exchange between the former standout wide receiver from USC and the official, London was caught in the middle of a scary play with 49ers safety Malik Mustapha, when the two collided  head-on and had a helmet-to-helmet play, resulting in London being evaluated for a concussion.

This isn’t the first time London has gone viral for his words.

In September, London got into a heated exchange that he claims got “personal” during a blowout loss to the Panthers.

Luckily for London, he was cleared to remain in the rest of the game after the hit and played a key part in helping his team get a 29-20 victory.

On the first play of the first quarter, London gave Atlanta a big time play when he caught a 21-yard touchdown reception to extend the Falcons’ lead to 26.

Atlanta’s defense held on in the fourth, forcing two turnovers. The first was when Brock Purdy threw an interception to Kendal Daniels at the 2:42 mark of the quarter.

Their next turnover came when safety Jesse Bates punched the ball out of George Kittle’s arm, setting up an Atlanta recovery.

The Falcons ran out the clock to end the game.

London finished as the team’s leading receiver, hauling in seven receptions for 66 yards and one touchdown.

WOW: WR Drake London، فوق ستاره #Falcons، پس از برخورد کلاه به کلاه در برابر #49ers، از کنار زمین به سمت داور فریاد زد "YOU A B*TCH". لندن به دنبال بازی خشمگین بود و خودداری نکرد. لندن عصبانی بود.
مشخص نیست لندن دقیقاً چه گفته است، اما گمانه زنی ها در رسانه های اجتماعی حاکی از آن است که او گفته است: "تو یک ب-ه!" ویدیو با صحبت لندن با یکی از اعضای سازمان شاهین ها در کنار خط شروع شد، سپس پایین آمد و در آخرین ثانیه سرش را به عقب برگرداند تا ناامیدی خود را به گوش مسئول اعلام کند. قبل از تبادل گرم بین گیرنده برجسته سابق USC و مقام رسمی، لندن در میانه یک بازی ترسناک با مالک مصطفی امنیت 49 نفر گرفتار شد، زمانی که این دو به صورت رو در رو با هم برخورد کردند و کلاه به کلاه بازی کردند و در نتیجه لندن به دلیل ضربه مغزی ارزیابی شد. این اولین باری نیست که لندن برای سخنان او در فضای مجازی منتشر می شود. در ماه سپتامبر، لندن با یک تبادل گرم مواجه شد که به ادعای او در جریان باخت به پانترز، "شخصی" شد. خوشبختانه برای لندن، او اجازه داده شد تا در ادامه بازی باقی بماند.

news.originalContent:
Church mourners die on Kenya’s Nairobi-Mombasa Highway weeks after another crash killed 17 people.

A bus carrying mourners has collided with a truck on a major highway in southeastern Kenya, killing at least 24 people, police say.

The crash happened in the Kanga area near Mtito Andei, on the road linking the capital, Nairobi, to the coastal city of Mombasa, at about 7:45am (04:45 GMT) on Sunday, October 25.

Another 24 people were injured, hospital officials said.

The deaths came just over three weeks after another crash on the highway killed 17 people, prompting fresh government promises to improve road safety.

The bus belonged to Power of the Word Church International in Mombasa and was taking passengers home from their pastor’s funeral in western Kenya.

They had stopped for breakfast shortly before the collision, according to one survivor.

The other vehicle was a truck transporting cement.

Violet Mwandonyi, who survived the crash, told the Associated Press on Sunday that she remembered passengers crying out for passing motorists to help.

She said she did not know what had happened to her two children, who had been travelling on the bus.

The cause of the crash remains under investigation.

Makueni County Commissioner Abdullahi Khalif, the government’s senior administrator in the area, told Kenyan newspaper The Standard that the bus driver had tried to overtake several vehicles before colliding with an oncoming truck.

Kenya’s National Transport and Safety Authority (NTSA) also identified dangerous overtaking as a possible cause. Another survivor said the truck struck the bus from behind.

On October 3, a crash involving several vehicles killed 17 people, most of them Catholic pilgrims travelling to a prayer site, near Salama on the same highway.

Police said a truck driver had tried to overtake another truck before the collision.

The NTSA had identified that stretch of road as an area with a history of crashes.

President William Ruto offered condolences on Sunday and ordered inspections of vehicles used for public transport.

Transport Minister Davis Chirchir said the government would step up enforcement against speeding and unsafe overtaking, improve dangerous sections of road and strengthen training and checks for commercial drivers.

In a statement on Sunday, Chirchir said the government would work with police, local authorities and lawmakers on the measures, including closer oversight of buses and heavy goods vehicles.

“We cannot continue treating road safety as business as usual,” he said, calling for stronger action to reduce deaths.

Figures from the NTSA, reported by Kenyan media, show that 5,009 people died in road crashes in 2025, with 2,150 deaths recorded in the first half of 2026.

The authority estimates that about 20,000 crashes occur across Kenya each year.

Following Sunday’s collision, it called for road crashes to be declared a national disaster.

news.originalContent:
ماریا کورینا ماچادو، رهبر مخالفان ونزوئلا، پس از بیش از ۱۰ ماه دوری از کشورش به ونزوئلا بازگشته است. بازگشت او در حالی صورت می‌گیرد که فضای سیاسی این کشور همچنان پرتنش است.

خانم ماچادو روز یکشنبه در شبکه اجتماعی ایکس نوشت: «من اینجا هستم؛ در کنار شما.»

ادماندو گونزالس اوروتیا، نامزد پیشین انتخابات ریاست‌جمهوری ونزوئلا و متحد خانم ماچادو، نیز چند دقیقه بعد این خبر را تأیید کرد و نوشت: «با خوشحالی به شما اعلام می‌کنم که رهبر ما، ماریا کورینای عزیزم، در خاک ونزوئلا حضور دارد.»

او افزود که به‌زودی در ونزوئلا به خانم ماچادو خواهد پیوست تا این کشور را به سوی «آزادی» پیش ببرند.

یکی از مشاوران خانم ماچادو در ماه سپتامبر گفته بود که او طی چند هفته پیش از آن، هفت بار برای بازگشت به ونزوئلا تلاش کرده، اما هر بار از ورودش جلوگیری شده بود.

هنوز مشخص نیست که خانم ماچادو پس از بازگشت چه برنامه‌ای دارد؛ با این حال، او پیش‌تر گفته بود که در صورت برگزاری انتخابات، بار دیگر نامزد ریاست‌جمهوری خواهد شد.

سخنگوی خانم ماچادو در بیانیه‌ای که در اختیار مارگارت برنان از شبکه خبری سی‌بی‌اس، شریک رسانه‌ای بی‌بی‌سی در آمریکا، قرار گرفت، بازگشت او را «گامی مهم در مسیر گذار دموکراتیک و برگزاری انتخابات ریاست‌جمهوری آزاد، عادلانه و قابل راستی‌آزمایی در آینده‌ای نزدیک» توصیف کرد.

ماریا کورینا ماچادو که از چهره‌های سرشناس مخالفان دولت مادورو است، در سال ۲۰۲۳ در انتخابات مقدماتی مخالفان برای تعیین نامزد ریاست‌جمهوری پیروز شد.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

این انتخابات مستقل از نهاد رسمی برگزاری انتخابات ونزوئلا برگزار شد و او بیش از ۹۰ درصد آرا را به دست آورد.

مقام‌های ونزوئلا پیش از برگزاری این انتخابات، خانم ماچادو را از نامزدی در انتخابات ریاست‌جمهوری سال ۲۰۲۴ محروم کرده بودند. آنها این تصمیم را با طرح اتهام‌هایی درباره تخلفات اداری و مالی و حمایت او از تحریم‌های آمریکا توجیه کردند.

خانم ماچادو این اتهام‌ها را رد کرد و محرومیت خود را دارای انگیزه‌های سیاسی دانست.

در انتخابات ریاست‌جمهوری سال ۲۰۲۴، ادموندو گونزالس اوروتیا، متحد خانم ماچادو، به‌جای او در برابر مادورو نامزد شد.

شورای ملی انتخابات ونزوئلا که با دولت مادورو همسو بود، او را برنده انتخابات اعلام کرد، اما جزئیات کامل شمارش آرا را منتشر نکرد.

در مقابل، مخالفان اعلام کردند که گونزالس پیروز انتخابات بوده است، نه مادورو. آنها برای اثبات ادعای خود نسخه‌هایی از صورت‌جلسه‌های شمارش آرا را منتشر کردند.

در سوم ژانویه ۲۰۲۶، چند هفته پس از آنکه خانم ماچادو ونزوئلا را ترک کرد و برای دریافت جایزه صلح نوبل به نروژ رفت، نیروهای آمریکایی در عملیاتی نظامی نیکلاس مادورو، رئیس‌جمهور وقت ونزوئلا، را بازداشت و به آمریکا منتقل کردند.

دولت دونالد ترامپ سپس از دلسی رودریگز، معاون مادورو، به‌عنوان رهبر ونزوئلا حمایت کرد.

خانم رودریگز به‌عنوان رئیس‌جمهور موقت سوگند یاد کرد و بعدتر توافقی نفتی با ایالات متحده امضا کرد.

news.originalContent:
Manchester United cheers Michael Carrick off after Bournemouth loss but booed Bruno Fernandes, what now for crisis club?

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick left the Old Trafford pitch on Sunday to the sound of his name being sung by the adoring home support, but he may never lead the team onto the field again.

His players followed him and the message delivered to them and the club captain Bruno Fernandes, who was an unused substitute, was quite different.

The 3-0 thumping by Bournemouth was a result that marked a 40-year low for the crisis club and plunged it to new depths – and the fans were determined to let United’s owners and playing staff know it.

The opening seven league matches marked United’s worst start since 1986. The latest defeat, their sixth of the season, leaves the club just a point above the relegation zone and without a win in eight matches in all competitions.

Fernandes, the Professional Footballers’ Association’s Player of the Year last season, was left among the substitutes on Sunday as a result of criticising Carrick after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation at Como in the UEFA Champions League.

The Portuguese player has been the Red Devils’ darling since he arrived in 2020, and seemed to have sealed his place as a club legend in a time of darkness with his accolade achieved on the back of United’s third-place finish, which they have only twice bettered in 13 years.

The award came as a result of his record number of assists in a Premier League season – all the more impressive in a side that lacked a spark anywhere else on the pitch.

The upturn in fortunes under Carrick’s interim position last term, when he replaced Ruben Amorim in January, resulted in his full-time appointment in the summer.

A tenure that may now have run its course, with him and United’s best player seemingly at loggerheads.

The United fans are famously loyal to their managers and players. Boos for anyone associated with the home side at Old Trafford were relatively unheard of until the last two seasons.

Now the boss receiving the adulation on exiting one of world football’s greatest stages – the Theatre of Dreams – may be the one on whom the curtain is being pulled.

Fernandes is no villain in this piece, but United’s fans have delivered a clear message directly to the heart of the dressing room – sending it via the player who could do no wrong in the eyes of the supporters will leave the ears of every member of the squad ringing.

Outplayed is one thing, but being outrun and outfought is another.

United’s history has been one of rebuilds and comebacks. They have known difficult days – their most successful manager Sir Alex Ferguson was on the verge of the sack in 1990 before winning the FA Cup and beginning one of the greatest runs of trophy-laden eras in football.

Their wait for a league title stretched from 1967 – and the Holy Trinity of George Best, Bobby Charlton and Denis Law – to 1993, when Ferguson’s inspired signing of Eric Cantona ignited glory days even the biggest club in the world at the time had never seen.

Now, United are on the edge of a precipice – quite literally if the gap to the drop zone is even to be realistically contemplated. Perhaps United’s cross-town rivals City won’t be the only Manchester club facing relegation this season.

That is demise no one is truly considering yet.

They are, however, at a crossroads – and the divide between Carrick and Fernandes – his captain, who criticised the tactics that stopped United pressing their Italian opponents in midweek, is likely to see the axe fall on the manager rather than a valuable asset.

“Manchester United need to make the change tonight (Sunday),” former England team-mate of Carrick, Jamie Carragher, told British broadcaster Sky Sports when asked if a sacking was needed.

“The fans have taken the side of the manager, which is not about him being the manager, it’s about him being a huge figure in United’s history – and those players have done nothing compared to teams of the past.

“So Carrick is always going to win that fight – and rightly so – with Fernandes, no matter how talented a player he is.

“But also United – one of the biggest clubs in the world – are 16th in the table right now and that can’t happen – it can’t continue and Carrick needs to be relieved of his duties.

“He wants to be sacked. It’s become untenable. He doesn’t want to be sat in the dugout with those players.

“Imagine going into training with Fernandes after not bringing him on? It’s a rancid dressing room. He wants to be put out of his misery.”

Gary Neville, former Manchester United defender and team-mate of Carrick’s for club and country, added: “Carrick is popular, but the owners, the sporting department and the players are not.

“They will probably make a decision that will disgust United fans, but it is probably necessary.

The final word of the day belongs to the man in the middle of a power battle that has seen him win the popular vote, but one that is unlikely to sway the United hierarchy.

“I take the responsibility,” Carrick said in the post-match news conference. “I totally understand the situation, I’m not expecting anything, I’m carrying on as normal and I love this place.”

In something of a reference to dropping the club captain and the response he received from the crowd at the end, Carrick continued: “I always do what I feel is going to be the best for the club, whatever decision is made.

“I’ve tried to do everything I can to not be in this position and for a number of reasons, whatever they are, we’ve not been able to stop that happening to the position we’re in.

“I’ve always felt that support and always felt that connection with the [fans].

“I have to say it is mixed emotions, I didn’t really expect that from the supporters. The respect that I have for them and for them to show that back meant an awful lot.”

Emotions are running high at Old Trafford and, even though Carrick denied it, his fanfare at the end may well prove to have been his farewell.

The Theatre of Dreams has become a house of horrors – for the 11th manager since Ferguson retired and with United’s last Premier League title now stretching back to 2013.

news.originalContent:
Student protests, police violence and French media obsessed with 'barbarians'.

What began as protests over education has rapidly taken over the streets of France and turned into one of the country’s biggest waves of unrest in years.

Many mainstream media outlets have focused their coverage on the violence and looting rather than on the demands of the demonstrators. A lot of airtime has fixated on who the protesters are and what they look like, often using racist terms. That narrative has been picked up by right-wing movements abroad.

Contributors:
Cole Stangler – author, Paris Is Not Dead, and lecturer, American College of the Mediterranean
Diane de Vignemont – Paris-based journalist
Harrison Stetler – lecturer and writer
Philippe Marliere – professor of French and European politics, University College London

Israel’s elections are just days away and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has reverted to a familiar alarmist tactic to consolidate support: hyping an “imminent” threat from Iran and telling the United States that it should “finish the job”. Meenakshi Ravi looks at the messaging.

More than four and a half years into Russia’s full-scale invasion, Ukraine remains under attack, and its journalists are forced to balance many responsibilities at once.

They are documenting a war that has become more dangerous than ever, countering Russian propaganda efforts and trying to hold their own government to account at a time when the news media have been expected to fall into line. The Kyiv Independent, an online newspaper, has been doing all three since 2021.

The Listening Post spoke with its editor-in-chief and cofounder Olga Rudenko about the pressures of reporting when your country is at war.

Featuring:
Olga Rudenko – editor-in-chief, The Kyiv Independent
news.content:
اعتراضات دانشجویی، خشونت پلیس و رسانه‌های فرانسوی که به "بربرها" وسواس دارند. آنچه که با اعتراضات علیه آموزش آغاز شد، به سرعت خیابان‌های فرانسه را فرا گرفت و به یکی از بزرگترین موج ناآرامی کشور در سال‌های اخیر تبدیل شد. بسیاری از رسانه‌های جریان اصلی پوشش خود را بر خشونت و غارت متمرکز کرده‌اند تا خواسته‌های تظاهرکنندگان. زمان زیادی از پخش به این موضوع پرداخته است که معترضان چه کسانی هستند و چگونه به نظر می رسند، اغلب از اصطلاحات نژادپرستانه استفاده می کنند. این روایت توسط جنبش‌های راست‌گرای خارج از کشور پذیرفته شده است. مشارکت‌کنندگان:
کول استانگلر - نویسنده، پاریس نمرده است، و مدرس کالج آمریکایی مدیترانه
دایان دو وینمون - روزنامه نگار مستقر در پاریس
هریسون استتلر - مدرس و نویسنده فیلیپ مارلیر - استاد سیاست فرانسه و اروپا، دانشگاه کالج لندن
انتخابات اسرائیل چند روز دیگر باقی مانده است و بنیامین نتانیاهو، نخست وزیر، به یک تاکتیک هشداردهنده آشنا برای تثبیت حمایت بازگشته است: تهدید "قریب الوقوع" ایران و گفتن به ایالات متحده که باید "کار را تمام کند". Meenakshi Ravi به پیام نگاه می کند. با گذشت بیش از چهار سال و نیم از تهاجم تمام عیار روسیه، اوکراین همچنان مورد حمله قرار می‌گیرد و روزنامه‌نگاران آن مجبور به تعادل در بسیاری از مسئولیت‌ها هستند. آن‌ها در حال مستندسازی جنگی هستند که خطرناک‌تر از همیشه شده است، با تلاش‌های تبلیغاتی روسیه مقابله می‌کنند و سعی می‌کنند دولت خود را در زمانی که انتظار می‌رفت رسانه‌های خبری درگیر آن شوند، بازخواست کنند.

news.originalContent:
Photo by Andrew Harnik/Getty Images

House Speaker Mike Johnson on Sunday defended Republicans’ record, arguing that the GOP offers American families stability and common-sense solutions even as widespread frustration over the cost of living threatens the party’s congressional majority ahead of the November midterms.

Johnson’s remarks during an interview with “Fox News Sunday” host Shannon Bream come as Republicans hope to retain control of the House despite polling showing respondents’ increasing dissatisfaction with President Donald Trump’s handling of the economy. The speaker has repeatedly touted his party’s legislative accomplishments while casting Democrats as a threat to economic stability.

“It’s not been easy, but we have an extraordinary record of delivering for the American people, fulfilling our promises,” Johnson, reflecting on his three-year speakership, said during the interview before listing various accomplishments. “You know, we effectively made a contract with America in 2024, and we have done everything that we said we were going to do. Secured the border tight. We gave the largest tax cut in U.S. history. We made the largest spending cut in U.S. history as well, $1.6 trillion to try to get the government to work more efficiently and effectively. We cut massive Biden-era regulations. We got the economy going again. We have Trump accounts for newborns, the first-ever nationwide school choice program. We have the lowest violent crime in 126 years. Biggest decline in prescription drug costs in 60 years. We got back to American energy dominance and peace through strength. We had a million jobs added in the private sector alone in the last 19 months. It goes on and on and on. We’re reshoring American manufacturing and we are fixing the economy we inherited under the last administration with 40-year high inflation.”

Americans face a simple question: what is best for me and my family, my children, and my aging parents?Republicans offer common sense solutions and a steady hand at the wheel — while the Democrats are going crazy.My full conversation with @ShannonBream on @FoxNewsSunday 📺👇 pic.twitter.com/9jelB4iPWO

Bream then asked if Republicans face a “messaging problem,” noting polls show rising concerns about economy.

“They don’t like the direction the country is moving in,” she pressed. “They feel very pessimistic. Is something lost in translation? Is there more work to be done?”

Johnson responded, citing a “hostile media environment” before acknowleding the economic concerns. “Gas prices are too high, we know that, and, of course, we have much more work to be done. But in a contrast election, the American people have a very simple choice: do you want to turn the government over, again, to the people who open the border, want to ban fossil fuels — what’s that going to do for gas prices, the people that don’t believe in the rule of law, the people that brought you the unsafe streets and the terrible economic conditions?”

“We have set the ship of state on the right course, and it’s got to be continued,” he added. “And if you look in these individual races, House races across the country, it’s a very simple decision. Every voter has to ask themselves a simple question, ‘Which candidate is best for me and my family, my children, my aging parents?’ In every one of these cases, the Republican is offering common sense solutions and a steady hand at the wheel. And the Democrats, increasingly, are going crazy. They really are. There’s an insurgent Marxist left that is taking over that party. And when we watch the videos of what’s happening in Paris and France and other countries in Europe right now, that’s a harbinger of things to come unless you keep the grown-ups in charge. And that’s what this election really is all about at the end of the day.”

Johnson’s outward confidence, however, contrasts with recent polling suggesting Republicans face significant obstacles in persuading voters that GOP policies have improved household finances.

An Oct. 15 Associated Press-NORC survey found that 84% of respondents consider the cost of living to be one of the most important issues influencing their midterm vote, while 85% identified the broader economy as a top concern. The same survey, meanwhile, found that 79% of respondents disapprove of Trump’s handling of the cost of living, while 74% disapprove of his management of the economy. In addition, nearly half of respondents, 47%, said they prefer Democrats control the House, compared with 38% who favor Republicans retaining their majority.

The findings illustrate the economic challenges confronting Republican candidates, particularly as voters continue to grapple with elevated household expenses and questions about whether Trump’s Washington has delivered meaningful financial relief.

Johnson has nevertheless maintained that Republicans can defy expectations in November, pointing to the party’s tax legislation and economic agenda as evidence that the GOP deserves to remain in power.

“We have incredible turnout,” Johnson previously claimed during an Oct. 18 Fox News interview. “It feels like 2024 to me when we defied the odds. I believe we can defy history and keep this majority.”

The speaker had also warned that Democratic control of Congress would bring higher prices and economic uncertainty, and argued that Democrats would attempt to reverse Republicans’ tax policies.

“If we turn this back over to Democrats right now, we know what the result would be,” Johnson said in the Oct. 18 interview. “It’d be chaos.”

Public dissatisfaction, however, appears to extend beyond partisan preferences.

An Oct. 1 AP-NORC poll found that 65% of U.S. adults blamed Trump’s policies for higher-than-usual prices, while 69% said his handling of the cost of living had been worse than expected.

That dissatisfaction included Republican respondents, 52% of whom said Trump’s performance on affordability has fallen short of their expectations.

A separate October AP-NORC survey found that voters trusted Democrats over Republicans to handle the cost of living, 38% to 27%, although another 27% said they trusted neither party.

With the Nov. 3 midterms approaching, Johnson has framed the election as a choice between two fundamentally different approaches to governing.

“This is a contrast election between common sense and crazy,” Johnson said Oct. 18. “And the American people are not signing up for crazy.”
